scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a "rollback" on r13, R11 reports it lost an EIGRP
neighbor and 113.1.x.x routes disappeared from R11's topology
table. R13 reports EIGRP is running and its config looks valid.
What changed?

injection.action: change EIGRP AS from 100 to 300 (a value R11 doesn't speak)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r13 EIGRP AS number
Mechanism: EIGRP requires both ends of an adjacency to share
  the same AS. R11 runs AS 100 (covering both R12 and R13
  sides per the collapsed-single-AS fix from earlier). R13
  was reconfigured to AS 300. Hello packets carry the AS,
  the mismatch is detected, and the adjacency never forms.
  R11 stops seeing 113.1.x routes, and R13 stops seeing
  102.x / 112.x / 120.x routes from R12 via R11.
Localization: r13
Root cause: EIGRP AS mismatch (R13 in AS 300, R11/R12 in AS 100)
Fix: re-configure r13 to AS 100
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: EIGRP AS number / EIGRP autonomous system

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the EIGRP process/AS configuration on r13. r11 and r13 are directly connected on the FF segment (r11 eth2 103.1.1.1/8 ↔ r13 eth0 103.1.1.2/8) and should form an EIGRP adjacency there to exchange the 113.1.x.x loopback routes hosted on r13.

Mechanism: EIGRP requires both sides to use the same autonomous system number. After the “rollback,” r13 is running EIGRP under AS 300, while r11 is running EIGRP under AS 100. This AS mismatch prevents neighbor formation on the FF link, so r11 stops learning the 113.1.x.x routes from r13 and they age out of the topology table.

Localization and evidence:
- r11 config: “router eigrp 100” with network 103.0.0.0/8 (r11 eth2) and “show ip eigrp interfaces” shows 0 peers on eth2; “show ip eigrp neighbors” lists only 112.1.1.2 on eth0, none on eth2.
- r13 config: “router eigrp 300” with network 103.0.0.0/8 and 113.1.x.x; “show ip eigrp neighbors” shows no neighbors.
- r13 carries 113.1.1.0/24–113.1.4.0/24 on loopbacks, matching the routes r11 reported losing.

Root cause: The rollback on r13 loaded an incorrect EIGRP autonomous system (AS 300 instead of AS 100), breaking adjacency with r11.

Corrective fix: Reconfigure r13 to run EIGRP in AS 100 (matching r11) and include the 103.0.0.0/8 and 113.1.x.x networks. After committing, verify “show ip eigrp neighbors” on both sides shows the peer on the 103.1.1.x link and confirm the 113.1.x.x routes reappear on r11.

The writeup explicitly instructs reconfiguring r13 to EIGRP AS 100 and advertising the 103.0.0.0/8 and 113.1.x.x networks, which matches the expected fix.
